events.title: The Abbasids execute the 42 captives of Amorium at Samarra
events.description: The Abbasids executed at Samarra 42 Byzantine officers and notables, taken hostage in the sack of Amorium in 838, after they refused to convert to Islam. Repeated Byzantine efforts to ransom them had been rebuffed.
events.html: The Abbasids executed at Samarra 42 Byzantine officers and notables, taken hostage in the sack of Amorium in 838, after they refused to convert to Islam. Repeated Byzantine efforts to ransom them had been rebuffed.

events.title: Philip II of France takes Château Gaillard
events.description: French troops captured Richard the Lionheart's great castle above the Seine after a six-month siege, some climbing in through a latrine chute. Normandy fell to France within months.
events.html: French troops captured Richard the Lionheart's great castle above the Seine after a six-month siege, some climbing in through a latrine chute. Normandy fell to France within months.

events.title: Tommaso Parentucelli is elected Pope Nicholas V
events.description: Meeting in the Roman basilica of Santa Maria sopra Minerva, the conclave elected Cardinal Tommaso Parentucelli to succeed Pope Eugene IV. He took the name Nicholas in memory of his obligations to Niccolò Albergati.
events.html: Meeting in the Roman basilica of Santa Maria sopra Minerva, the conclave elected Cardinal Tommaso Parentucelli to succeed Pope Eugene IV. He took the name Nicholas in memory of his obligations to Niccolò Albergati.

events.title: President Monroe signs the Missouri Compromise
events.description: Missouri was to enter the Union as a slave state and Maine as a free one, with slavery barred from the rest of the Louisiana Purchase north of 36°30'. The balance held for three decades.
events.html: Missouri was to enter the Union as a slave state and Maine as a free one, with slavery barred from the rest of the Louisiana Purchase north of 36°30'. The balance held for three decades.

events.title: The Alamo falls to Santa Anna
events.description: Mexican troops stormed the mission at dawn after a 13-day siege, killing nearly all of its roughly 200 defenders, including Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett. 'Remember the Alamo' became the Texan battle cry.
events.html: Mexican troops stormed the mission at dawn after a 13-day siege, killing nearly all of its roughly 200 defenders, including Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett. 'Remember the Alamo' became the Texan battle cry.

events.title: US Supreme Court decides Dred Scott v. Sandford
events.description: Chief Justice Roger Taney ruled that Black Americans could not be citizens and that Congress could not ban slavery in the territories. The decision deepened the crisis that led to civil war.
events.html: Chief Justice Roger Taney ruled that Black Americans could not be citizens and that Congress could not ban slavery in the territories. The decision deepened the crisis that led to civil war.

events.title: Clarence Birdseye's frozen foods go on sale
events.description: Shops in Springfield, Massachusetts, began selling quick-frozen vegetables, fruit, fish and meat using Birdseye's process. Frozen food went on to transform shopping and diets.
events.html: Shops in Springfield, Massachusetts, began selling quick-frozen vegetables, fruit, fish and meat using Birdseye's process. Frozen food went on to transform shopping and diets.

events.title: Ghana becomes independent
events.description: The Gold Coast became independent as Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah, the first sub-Saharan colony to win independence from a European power after the war. It inspired independence movements across Africa.
